VERIFIED_FACT—documented memory overlap: Operational Memory is a deterministic-first, provenance-linked acceleration layer with blob-compatibility states and shadow procedural candidates. Merged changes are explicitly not proof of causal effectiveness. SEL is private, optional and selective; global automatic retrieval remains HOLD, and SEL unavailability must not block otherwise executable source-first work. Neither requires a new vector-memory owner.

VERIFIED_FACT—documented verification/data boundaries: consumer receipts, exact-head/readback references, transition/completion bindings and append-only convergence evidence already provide verification building blocks. Restricted evidence requires immutable private commit/path/hash/schema/completeness bindings; unavailable required authority stays unavailable. Permanent governance separates source-destructive from recovery-destructive authority. These are documented defenses, not proof that credentials and every runtime path enforce them.
hypotheses: PROPOSAL | BUILD_NOTHING is the current comparison default, not a proven optimum. Existing owners already cover nearly all named components. Its falsifier would be a reproducible class of eligible missions that existing callbacks/reconciliation cannot advance despite available evidence, an authorized executor and satisfied owner gates—not merely a large queue or old issue.

PROPOSAL | Completion-verifier-only is the first minimal alternative worth evaluating. A derived mission view could reference existing requirement coverage, post-fix/convergence evidence, durable readback and consumer receipts without minting new completion authority. Its marginal value depends on demonstrably detecting false closure or explaining unresolved coverage beyond what existing verifiers already provide.

PROPOSAL | A minimal bounded continuation extension is plausible only after a specific missing edge is established. It would remain inside the Supervisor, reference existing owner task identities and queues, and reconsider work only after relevant evidence changes. Owner-gated, blocked, cancelled, superseded and budget-limited states would remain distinct from independently verified completion. It would not authorize this API component to execute.

PROPOSAL | Continuation safety can be evaluated against replay fixtures: duplicate event delivery, crash after an effect but before acknowledgement, changed owner/task hash, late completion after cancellation, supersession during execution, unavailable private evidence and ambiguous timeout. A defensible design preserves original evidence, prevents stale effects and distinguishes uncertain execution from a safe retry. Existing delegation/run limits remain ceilings.

PROPOSAL | A separate mission service is currently the weaker alternative: it adds deployment, state synchronization, callback, credential and duplicate-owner risks without supplied incremental-value evidence. A persistent orchestrator is still less justified. Evidence that a particular source needs persistent collection infrastructure does not establish that general mission orchestration needs a persistent service.

PROPOSAL | Marginal-value comparison should retain a fixed denominator of unique eligible missions, including failures and non-completion terminal states. Useful measures include time to independently verified and consumed closure, false-completion rate, duplicate effects, unresolved requirement coverage, repeated-investigation burden, total inference/rework cost and writer-queue delay. Blocked/cancelled/superseded work must not inflate completion success.

PROPOSAL | Existing-owner review boundaries remain sufficient: orchestration/Supervisor for wakeups and routing; remediation/Codex owners for task identity and post-fix closure; API governance for task validation and budget admission; research governance for scientific transitions; data-boundary owners for private receipts; repository safety governance for destructive-authority separation. These are advisory evaluation routes, not write requests or authorization.
